assumptions: Order-level success rate means the share of orders with at least one successful attempt.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 89.63%, order-level 92.28%, technical 93.37%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap between them.

facts.text: Order-level success rate for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30 was 92.28%, with 316,628 successful orders out of 343,111 total orders.

The same period shows different success rates depending on the denominator: attempt-level 89.63% (316,628 of 353,242 attempts), order-level 92.28% (316,628 of 343,111 orders), and technical 93.37% (316,628 of 339,128).
The gap between the lowest and highest definition is 3.73 percentage points.
The data-quality scan found no issues (0 findings) across the attempts and dimension tables.

response.headline: The order-level success rate in September 2026 was 92.3%: 316,628 of 343,111 orders had at least one successful attempt.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the distribution of attempts per order and the share of failed attempts that belong to orders that eventually succeeded.
hypotheses.rationale: There are 353,242 attempts for 343,111 orders, so there are more attempts than orders, which is consistent with retries.
hypotheses.text: The attempt-level rate is lower than the order-level rate because some orders needed more than one attempt, and failed retries count against the attempt-level rate.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review the technical success rate definition and list the orders that are excluded from its denominator.
hypotheses.rationale: Its denominator (339,128) is smaller than the order count (343,111) while the numerator is the same.
hypotheses.text: The technical success rate is higher than the order-level rate because it excludes some orders or attempts, such as customer drop-offs, from its denominator.

recommendations.rationale: The three definitions differ by up to 3.73pp for the same month.
recommendations.text: State the denominator whenever quoting the September success rate (for example 'order-level 92.28%') so numbers are not compared across definitions.

recommendations.rationale: More attempts than orders suggests retries influence the gap between attempt-level and order-level rates.
recommendations.text: Analyse retry behaviour (attempts per order and retry success) to see how much recoverable failure there is.
